messages:
anya: quick heads-up — canary for the int4+fp8 mixed rollout is showing a 12-18% tail-latency regression on long-seq (8k+) LLM traces. noticed after the kernel swap yesterday.

mike: ugh. same batcher config? or did we change kernel selection policy?

anya: batcher config unchanged. runtime picked a `fused_int4_attn_v2` kernel for layers 7-18 because of throughput heuristics. fallback to fp8 kernel for other layers.

liu: do we have profiler traces? curious if KV cache warmup or KV-copying is contributing.

anya: attaching short snippet from pprof run (canary node):

```
# p99 latency by op (sample)
attn_forward_fused_int4  82ms
attn_forward_fp8        62ms
kv_read                 12ms
batcher_overhead        9ms
```

mike: that order suggests the fused int4 attn kernel has worse long-seq scaling (maybe memory-bound for long KV). did we change per-channel calibration for int4?

anya: yep — for int4 we switched to per-tensor symmetric range by default to stabilize quant minima. planning doc said per-channel would be noisier for some layers.

sam: per-tensor is cheaper but for attention heads per-channel often preserves head-level dynamics. outliers in activation distributions can collapse some heads if per-tensor.

nina: also worth checking the calibration dataset. we used a short-context web-scrape sample set (avg len 400). that underrepresents long-tail contexts.

mike: bingo. calibration set bias -> quant scale too small for long-ctx activations -> kernel needs extra corrective ops (saturations?) -> throughput hit.

perf-bot: reminder: open perf regression ticket created — PF-8823. Link: https://redwood.internal/pf/8823

liu: proposal: run a small re-calibration sweep where we: (1) include 5k+ long-context examples (2) mark extreme activations as outliers and clip at 99.999th percentile per-channel (3) compare per-channel vs per-tensor scales on a per-layer basis.

anya: can we test technique without re-quantizing model for every variant? maybe runtime assist via dynamic rescale for layers with high KV magnitude?

sam: dynamic rescale maybe a stopgap. real fix is better calibration sampling and per-channel scales on layers where head variance > threshold. we should add a per-layer heuristic: if head_std_ratio > 4 then use per-channel; otherwise per-tensor.

nina: agreed. but how do we pick the threshold? previous runs used 3.0 and it flipped 20% of layers. I suggest we produce a small scoring script that outputs: layer, head_std, head_mean, outlier_count, suggested-mode.

mike: also check kernel memory access pattern. `fused_int4_attn_v2` assumes packed KV layout; if per-channel scales vary, unpack/repacks might occur and cost us memory bandwidth on 8k sequences.

anya: action items I can take today:
- add 2k long-context samples to the calibration corpus (mix between dialogues and code)
- run calibration sweep per-tensor vs per-channel for top-6 layers
- collect pprof traces and heatmaps for kv_read / attn kernels

mike: I'll instrument the runtime to log when it applies an on-the-fly rescale and measure extra cycles.

liu: I'll write the scoring script for head_std_ratio and run it on the model checkpoints we used in canary.

nina: +1. also let's log any samples that trigger >1e6 activations for auditing (possible outliers).

sam: quick note: for FP8 candidates, quant noise behaves differently; mixing int4+fp8 may expose numeric cliff edges where small pre-quant shifts cause big kernel branching. include mixed-precision-only traces.

anya: thanks all. I'll post results in this thread once the sweeps finish (couple hrs). if anyone wants to pair on heuristics, ping me. :eyes:

mike: thanks — if we can get a reproducible perf run, we can consider a short rollback of the kernel swap on high-latency routes until calibration is validated. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: regression ticket PF-8823 updated with initial traces by anya at 1719876600.

anya: posted preliminary calibration diffs -> early sign per-channel on layers 8/12 fixes most of p99 regression (reduces attn_forward_fused_int4 from 82ms -> 58ms) — posting full pprof in ~30m.

sam: amazing if that holds. if so, we'll update default calibration policy to per-channel for attention blocks and keep per-tensor elsewhere. will need to notify devex/docs.

nina: also add a note in the runbook about sampling corpus: always include at least 1% long-context (>4k) and 0.1% extreme-token sequences (e.g., code dumps) to catch distributional drift.

anya: noted. will draft runbook change in a PR.

mike: great work. keep the canary pinned until we verify.

anya: will do.
